mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.1% indicates accommodative monetary policy that compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced cost of capital for corporate valuation.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.1% (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Unemployment spikes correlate with 5-day equity drawdowns
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly increases in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal income (RSAFS) above 0.5% signal robust consumer demand, elevating corporate earnings expectations and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% in 1 month
evidence_refs: fact:Joint demand indicators predict 20-day equity returns
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS rise > 0.5% (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, CPIAUCSL monthly increases exceeding 0.5% signal inflationary pressures that trigger Federal Reserve tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >50% of late-cycle periods when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).

mechanism_narrative: Non-farm payrolls exceeding 140 million indicate a strong labor market that sustains consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Payroll growth > 140M correlates with 60-day equity gains
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >50% of periods when PAYEMS > 140 million (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production declining below 106.0 indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and profit margins, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when INDPRO < 106.0 (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous GDP growth above 1.5% annualized and housing starts rising above 0.5% signal synchronized economic expansion that boosts equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 1.5% and HOUST rises > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when GDPC1 > 1.5% and HOUST > 0.5% (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: In tight labor markets (UNRATE < 5.0%), a monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals economic fragility that reduces consumer confidence and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >50% of tight labor market periods when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).
